content: Steri-Strips are adhesive-backed surgical strips made of paper tape that are applied across an incision or minor cut. Their primary function is to hold the edges of a wound together during the healing process. These strips were developed by the company 3M. Steri-Strips can sometimes be used as an alternative to sutures (stitches) for certain injuries. They are preferred in some cases because they reduce scarring and are easier to manage in terms of wound care. The precursor to the Steri-Strip was Micropore Surgical Tape. There have been notable cases where Micropore Surgical Tape was used in extraordinary circumstances. For example, it was successfully employed to hold large abdominal incisions together when the patient’s skin was too fragile to tolerate sutures. In another case, the tape was used to reconstruct a patient’s abdominal wall and save their life when sutures failed to keep the wound closed due to compromised skin integrity. These dramatic outcomes prompted 3M to modify Micropore Surgical Tape by cutting it into strips of one-eighth inch, one-fourth inch, and one-half inch widths, sterilizing it, and packaging it for use as primary surface closures for incisions. Steri-Strips are not suitable for use over joints, as the movement in these areas can compromise their effectiveness. However, they are particularly useful in areas where the skin is thin and where sutures might cut through the tissue. To enhance the adhesive properties of Steri-Strips, tincture of benzoin can be applied to the dry skin surrounding the wound before application.
